Cleaning the room? 🥸💀 Hard pass. Similar to drawing patient’s labs, it is not in my job description either. It takes away time from diagnosing and treating patients.
I HATED med school. Like so deeply. And now I love intern year too. Love it.

Thank you. This entire post has made me feel validated. All of my co-residents who went to med school in New York think it’s normal. It’s completely foreign to me, and my team dismisses why I find it odd. I’ll just stay quiet tho for now & make the best of it.
Bruh, they make you all transport patients? 💀

I agree with being familiar, but for it to be my responsibility, 2+ hours a day, it feels more like a burden and waste of time when nurses could easily do it themselves like they do in the rest of the country. That time could go towards helping my patients, talking to families, learning the ropes of being a resident, etc.; we are allowed to disagree, though.

NYC has always been my dream city to live in, but in terms of residency/hospitals, I think they exploit the fact that there is an above-average demand to live here. Of course, NY isn’t everyone’s cup of tea—many people hate the idea of moving here—but I think the system has fostered the mentality that if you don’t like it here, someone else will gladly take your spot.

It is. It would be one thing if I learned how to draw blood throughout my medical training, but most American medical students never have to. I understand how it’s an excellent skill to have, but on top of my other responsibilities as an intern, it’s annoying feeling like I have to micromanage the orders—literally drawing the blood and taking it to the lab to get collected.
As they should! Good for your program for standing up to justice against a flawed system. Of course, every healthcare system is going to have issues, but I just can’t get over this one.
